source.title: Measuring and Controlling Solution Degeneracy across Task-Trained Recurrent Neural Networks
source.authors: Ann C. Huang; S. H. Singh; Flavio Martinelli; Kanaka Rajan

record.tranche_reason: The study tests whether independently initialized networks become more similar under changes in network width and other conditions, using RNN dynamics, weights, and SVCCA rather than the original studies’ representation-similarity measures.
record.gate_note: The paper reports cited findings about convergence in other work, which are not recorded as results. The paper’s own results include figure-only trends, for which the text supplies qualitative directions. Behavioral OOD variability is discussed but is not treated as a direct measurement of representation similarity.
record.test_reason: The study measures how similar the neural dynamics (DSA) and representations (SVCCA) are across 50 independently seeded RNNs of one architecture. It varies task complexity, feature learning, width and regularization. That is a different method aimed at V3 (cross-seed convergence), and at V1 only through width scaling within one architecture. The authors frame the width result as 'convergence-with-scale' and cite the Platonic paper. Weight-distance and OOD-behaviour measures are not representation alignment.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. Task complexity and stronger feature learning reduce dynamical degeneracy but increase weight degeneracy. Larger networks and structural regularization reduce degeneracy at dynamics, weights and behaviour. Behavioural effects are mixed: complexity reduces OOD variability, while feature learning increases it, possibly through overfitting. The authors present the width result as extending 'convergence-with-scale' to RNN dynamics, and note that SVCCA representational similarity is not constrained by the same factors.
record.recipe_differences: Uses DSA for dynamics, permutation-invariant Frobenius distances for weights, and SVCCA for static representations; the study concerns task-trained RNN solution degeneracy rather than the original studies’ representation-similarity procedures.
record.method_sensitivity: Outcomes differ by level of analysis: dynamical, weight, representational, and OOD behavioral degeneracy do not respond uniformly. DSA distance scale depends on hyperparameters, which the authors hold fixed within each task. In a standard-parameterization width sweep, unstable and lazier learning in the widest N-Bit Flip-Flop model coincides with an exception to the width trend.

fits_no_version.finding: Task complexity, memory demand, auxiliary loss and feature learning increase permutation-invariant recurrent-weight distance across seeds. Width and regularization decrease it. Weight-level dispersion can move opposite to dynamical convergence.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Cross-seed convergence of function or dynamics can coexist with divergent connectivity (weight-level degeneracy), with contravariant versus covariant factors.

fits_no_version.finding: Variability of OOD (temporal-generalization) loss across seeds falls with task complexity, width and regularization, but rises with stronger feature learning, decoupling from dynamical convergence.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Convergent internal dynamics on training data do not guarantee convergent OOD behaviour across models.

record.code_released: Code is stated to be attached as supplemental materials; no URL stated.
record.problems: Most reported degeneracy trends are available here only as plots, without exact values in the text. The experiments use task-trained RNNs and do not test cross-architecture, cross-objective, cross-dataset, or cross-modal alignment. SVCCA results are described qualitatively without absolute alignment values. The authors note that DSA distance scale depends on hyperparameters.

untested.parts: Different architectures, objectives, data or modalities. Capability as distinct from width. Sizes beyond 512 units. A readable SVCCA (static representation) trend with width.
All of it: no vision or language models and no paired image-caption data.
An absolute level of shared features or subspaces; only relative degeneracy across conditions is reported. Unit-level matching of activations.
All of it: no mapping-loss, stitching, relative-representation or unpaired alignment results.
All of it: no interpretable features or circuits are compared.
Sweeps of DSA or SVCCA hyperparameters (DSA hyperparameters are held fixed). Effects of changing the input data on similarity.
All of it: no plateau test, no cross-model comparison, and no test of whether shared data or objectives explain convergence rather than a common model of reality.

missing.what: Per-factor SVCCA representational-distance values, including the trend with network size
Standard-parameterization width sweep showing lower dynamical degeneracy with width on tasks other than 3BFF
Dense 12-width sweep (32–512 units) on 3BFF confirming lower dynamical degeneracy with width
GRUs on Sine Wave Generation: more channels lower cross-seed dynamical degeneracy, as in vanilla RNNs
Lorenz 96 chaotic task: all four factors, including width, shift dynamical degeneracy as in Table 1

record.verdict_notes: All rows compare same-architecture seeds on the same task, so V1 is tested only in a narrow form (width, with no cross-architecture comparison). V3 is the main version tested. The Contravariance Principle (harder tasks fewer solutions) resembles the Platonic paper's multitask argument, but no row tests V7's alternative-cause claim, so V7 links were removed. Most results are figure-only, giving relative trends without absolute similarity levels.

versions.untested_parts: Tests changes in width among task-trained RNNs; does not compare different architectures, objectives, datasets, or modalities, and does not establish that larger networks are more capable.
No vision-language models or paired image-caption representations.
Measures SVCCA subspace similarity across networks but does not report whether particular individual features or units recur.
No mapping, stitching, relative-representation, or unpaired alignment test.
No interpretable features or circuits are identified or compared.
Compares dynamical and static representational degeneracy and discusses training-task versus OOD behavior, but does not sweep DSA hyperparameters or systematically vary input datasets.
Studies task-trained RNNs sharing task conditions; does not test whether shared training data or objectives cause cross-model alignment, nor whether alignment plateaus as scale increases.

rows.measure: Average pairwise DSA distance between networks’ neural dynamics
rows.value: figure only; text reports that dynamical degeneracy decreased consistently across all tasks as complexity increased
